 Wall Street closed the week mixed as a sharp spike in volatility reflected fresh tech struggles, while investors continued to digest hotter-than-expected CPI data and the latest bank earnings.

CPI inflation heated up in September. On a year-over-year basis, the Consumer Price Index rose 3.7%, matching the consensus forecast and accelerating from a 3.4% gain in August.The Cboe Volatility Index ( VIX ) surged roughly 30% on Friday afternoon to trade above 21, reaching a more than four-month high as tech stocks continued to struggle.

Big banks kicked off Q3 earnings season as traders digested results from Goldman Sachs ( GS ), JPMorgan ( JPM ), Citigroup ( C ), Wells Fargo ( WFC ), and other major lenders.

For the week, the blue-chip Dow ( DJI ) added +0.67%, the benchmark S&P ( SP500 ) lost -1.95%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( C OMP:IND) plunged -4.48%. Read a preview of next week's major events in Seeking Alpha's Catalyst Watch .


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Outlook
 
 
 
 'Wrecking ball' 
 
 
 
Seeking Alpha
 
 
The UN is sounding the alarm on this year's El Niño, with the agency's emergency relief chief Tom Fletcher describing it as "a wrecking ball" that will bring extreme heat, droughts and floods. While El Niño is a normal climate pattern, it's expected to be unprecedented this year. This year appears similar to the 1997-98 event that caused an estimated $5.7T in global income losses. Read more. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Seeking Alpha's Calls Of The Week
 
 
 
Upgrading AppLovin ( APP ): Stock Has Fallen Too Far .

Papa John's ( PZZA ): Reset Paves Way For Recovery .

Patient Traders Can Start Buying  Winnebago ( WGO ).

 CII's  Distribution Is Likely Covered Through 2027 .

 RWTQ  Is Priced For Default, It's  Time To Buy .

Netflix ( NFLX ): I Was So Wrong, I Want To Cry .

Realty Income ( O ) May Be In Trouble, I'm Holding .

Red Cat's ( RCAT ) Steyr Deal Raises Dilution Risk .

AeroVironment ( AVAV ) Still Overvalued: It's A 'Sell.' 

Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ): Macau Weakness Persists .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 U.S. Indices 
Dow +0.4% to 52,215. S&P 500 -0.5% to 7,624. Nasdaq -0.7% to 25,955. Russell 2000 +2% to 2,776. CBOE Volatility Index -2.7% to 19.45. 

 S&P 500 Sectors 
Consumer Staples +0.5%. Utilities +0.8%. Financials +0.7%. Telecom -6.2%. Healthcare +1.5%. Industrials -1.9%. Information Technology -0.3%. Materials -0.1%. Energy +1.6%. Consumer Discretionary +0.5%. Real Estate +1.1%. 

 World Indices 
London -1.8% to 10,690. France -2.2% to 7,783. Germany -1.7% to 25,182. Japan -4% to 62,693. China -0.7% to 3,690. Hong Kong -4.5% to 23,093. India -2.2% to 73,124. 

 Commodities and Bonds 
Crude Oil WTI +4.5% to $103.44/bbl. Gold -4.1% to $4,010./oz. Natural Gas -15.6% to 2.63. Ten-Year Bond Yield -0.2 bps to 4.988. 

 Forex and Cryptos 
EUR/USD -0.33%. USD/JPY -0.74%. GBP/USD +0.36%. Bitcoin -0.8%. Litecoin -2.7%. Ethereum -0.8%. XRP -0.1%. 

 Top S&P 500 Gainers 
Hashbro ( HAS ) +19%. Charles River Laboratories ( CRL ) +15%. Roper Technologies ( ROP ) +14%. Allegion ( ALLE ) +14%. CrowdStrike Holdings ( CRWD ) +13%. 

 Top S&P 500 Losers 
Comfort Systems USA ( FIX ) -19%. Howmet Aerospace ( HWM ) -16%. Flex ( FLEX ) -15%. Quanta Services ( PWR ) -14%. Lam Research ( LRCX ) -13%.
